title: Linear combinations of random variables
overview: Find the expectation and variance of sums and differences of independent random variables. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Find expectations of affine and linear combinations.
Find variances of scaled variables and independent sums/differences.
Combine independent Poisson variables where the result remains Poisson.

definitions.definition: Knowledge of one variable gives no information about the other; required for adding variances here.
A dependence measure; it is zero for independent variables, explaining the syllabus variance rule.
A distribution family stays in the same family after a stated operation.

sections.title: Expectation rules
content: Expectation is linear whether or not variables are independent: E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b and E(aX+bY)=aE(X)+bE(Y). A constant shifts the mean directly.
bullets: A negative coefficient subtracts the corresponding mean.
Independence is not needed for expectation.

sections.title: Variance rules
content: Var(aX+b)=a²Var(X); adding a constant changes no spread. For independent X,Y, Var(aX+bY)=a²Var(X)+b²Var(Y). The variances add even for X−Y because (−1)²=1.
bullets: Do not subtract variances for a difference.
Independence is essential for the syllabus formula.

sections.title: Normal combinations
content: If X and Y are independent normal variables, aX+bY is normal with mean aμₓ+bμᵧ and variance a²σₓ²+b²σᵧ². State the complete distribution before calculating a probability.
bullets: Standard deviations do not add directly.
A shift changes mean but not variance.

sections.title: Poisson combinations
content: If independent X~Po(λ) and Y~Po(μ), then X+Y~Po(λ+μ). A difference is not Poisson. Splitting and combining counts requires independence and compatible intervals.
bullets: Only sums preserve the Poisson form here.
The parameters carry the same interval units.

examTips: Build the mean and variance on separate lines before standardising.
Square every scale factor in a variance calculation.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Adding standard deviations instead of variances.
Using the independent-variance rule without independence.

quickRecall.question: What is Var(X−Y) for independent X,Y?
What does adding a constant do to variance?
quickRecall.answer: Nothing; it shifts every value equally.

quickRecall.question: Is X−Y Poisson when X and Y are Poisson?
quickRecall.answer: No. Only the independent sum has the stated Poisson closure property.
